official_text: Every person, above four years of age, driving or riding or being carried on a motorcycle of any class or description shall, while in a public place, wear protective headgear conforming to such standards as may be prescribed by the Central Government.

official_text: A person who drives a motor vehicle at a speed or in a manner dangerous to the public, having regard to all the circumstances, is punishable for a first offence with imprisonment up to one year and/or fine up to five thousand rupees, and for a subsequent offence within three years with imprisonment up to two years and/or fine up to ten thousand rupees.

official_text: A person who drives a motor vehicle while having, per a breath analyser test, more than 30 milligrams of alcohol per 100 millilitres of blood, or while under the influence of a drug to an extent that renders him incapable of exercising proper control, is punishable for a first offence with imprisonment up to six months and/or a fine of ten thousand rupees, with enhanced imprisonment and/or fine for a repeat offence within three years.

official_text: Whoever causes the death of a person by rash or negligent driving of a motor vehicle, not amounting to culpable homicide, and reports the accident to a police officer or Magistrate soon after the occurrence, shall be punished with imprisonment for a term which may extend to five years, and shall also be liable to fine.

official_text: Where a driver causing death by rash or negligent driving escapes from the scene without reporting the accident to a police officer or Magistrate soon after the occurrence, the driver shall be punished with imprisonment for a term which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine.
plain_english: This provision sets out the legal rule or requirement stated in the source text. In practical terms: Fleeing the scene of a fatal accident without reporting it carries a substantially harsher maximum sentence (up to 10 years) than staying and reporting.
